title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Consolidated Balance Sheets (December 31, 2022 and 2021)
key_points: Total liabilities reported on the consolidated balance sheet at December 31, 2022 were $203,643 million (2021: $166,371 million).

The consolidated balance sheet liability line items for 2022 were: Customer deposits $110,239 million; Accounts payable $12,133 million; Short-term borrowings $1,348 million; Long-term debt $42,573 million; Other liabilities $37,350 million.
Customer deposits of $110,239 million is the largest single liability line item, exceeding the next-largest item (Long-term debt, $42,573 million) by about $67.7 billion.
Total assets were $228,354 million and total shareholders' equity was $24,711 million at December 31, 2022, so total liabilities plus equity equals total assets ($203,643 + $24,711 = $228,354).
Long-term debt of $42,573 million includes $12,662 million of debt issued by consolidated variable interest entities.

title: American Express 2022 10-K — MD&A Deposit Programs
key_points: 存款由美国银行子公司 American Express National Bank (AENB) 吸收，受 FDIC 保险，每账户持有人至少 $250,000。
AENB 直接零售存款（FDIC 保险的高收益储蓄账户与 CDs）是主要存款产品渠道，直接面向消费者。
AENB 亦提供支票账户产品，并按需通过第三方分销渠道吸收存款以满足整体融资目标。
截至 2022 年 12 月 31 日存款为 $110.2 billion。
2022 年任何时点均无商业票据（commercial paper）在外流通。
未来短期借款规模取决于融资策略、需求与市场状况。
raw_excerpt: We offer deposits within our U.S. bank subsidiary, AENB. These funds are currently insured up to an amount that is at least $250,000 per account holder through the FDIC. … Direct retail deposits offered by AENB is our primary deposit product channel, which makes FDIC-insured high-yield savings account and certificates of deposit (CDs) products available directly to consumers. AENB also offers checking account products and sources deposits through third-party distribution channels as needed to meet our overall funding objectives. As of December 31, 2022, we had $110.2 billion in deposits. … We had no commercial paper outstanding at any point during 2022.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Business Environment (2022 volume and loan growth context)
key_points: Worldwide network volumes increased 21 percent in 2022 versus the prior year (24 percent on an FX-adjusted basis).
Billed business increased 23 percent year-over-year (25 percent FX-adjusted) and represented 86 percent of total network volumes.
Card Member loans increased 22 percent year-over-year, with the majority of growth coming from existing Card Members.
Net interest income increased 28 percent versus the prior year, primarily driven by growth in Card Member loans.
The rising interest rate environment had a fairly neutral impact on full-year 2022 results, but rising rates had a modest negative impact on net interest income toward the end of the year.
